title: Citadel of Ricks — Master Schematic Database
generated_from: Evidence registers in this repository (see SCHEMATIC.md for derivation rules)

units.U: 1 U = R = equatorial radius of the central lens (the widest point of the main body). All lengths are multiples of U.
units.absolute_conversion_status: PROVISIONAL — see SCALE_1_TO_1.md. The show never states a size; 2,000 m is the mid-point of the evidence chain (1,500–3,000 m).

stl_alignment.note: translate by -centre, -equator_z; scale 1/36.33; rotate -36 deg about Z so pod A sits on +X (az 0)

coordinate_system.origin: Centre of the central lens at its equatorial plane (widest point of the main body). The main city deck is this plane.
coordinate_system.x: horizontal; +X = 'east' (used only for the East Sanchez Heights name-inference, confidence C)
coordinate_system.y: horizontal; +Y = 90 deg counter-clockwise from +X viewed from above
coordinate_system.z: Citadel vertical axis; +Z up (towards dome apex), -Z down into the lower metallic body
coordinate_system.azimuth: degrees, measured counter-clockwise from +X when viewed from +Z

placement_classes.LOCKED: Existence A and geometry directly supported. Do not move without new direct evidence.
placement_classes.ANCHORED: Existence A; position follows from an explicit source relationship (e.g. 'central plaza'). Move only if a frame contradicts it.
placement_classes.PROVISIONAL: Existence A/B; position is a reasoned inference (C). Expected to move once images are camera-matched.
placement_classes.PLACEHOLDER: Existence A/B/C; position is arbitrary (D) and exists only so the node has a slot in the model. Must be re-placed from images.
placement_classes.UNPLACED: Not given coordinates. Comic-only, prop-scatter, or no spatial evidence at all.

nodes.name: Central lens — lower hull

features: cyan rim light strips at the equator

nodes.rationale: STL cross-sections: the underside of the main body is the lower half of the lens, 0.10 R deep at the centre. The v2 "thin plate" was the right thickness but the wrong shape. Geometry measured from the STL.

nodes.name: Under-hub (keel mount block)

features: fins hang from its lower rim

nodes.rationale: In #23 a faceted block sits under the centre of the drum and the keel fins hang from it. It is the natural volume for the Drive stack (V-2/V-3). Depth is a ratio estimate. Silhouette fit: r 0.34, z -0.02 → -0.45. STL: below the lens the central section shrinks linearly from r 0.46 at −0.11 to 0.23 at −0.36.
unknowns: whether it is one block or several

nodes.name: Keel fin 1 of 5

tangential width ≈0.26 R at the root, ≈0.15 R at the tip

nodes.name: Central spike (energy blade)

features: central spike, r 0.19 at the root, 0.026 over the last 0.7 R

nodes.rationale: Third pass on #23, measured: keel top width ≈ 70 px = 0.87 R across; blade tip 125 px = 1.56 R below the disc underside; fins end ≈ 1.2 R down. The keel is a bright cyan crystalline blade on the axis flanked by flat plated fins with angled tips, all hanging from the under-hub. Existence A, ratios B. Numeric fit to #23: blade tip at z −2.10 (measured from the disc centre, not the front rim — the earlier 1.56 was measured from the wrong edge). Silhouette fit: blade root r 0.117, tip z -2.13. STL: central spike tip at 2.13 R below the equator — identical to the silhouette-fitted blade tip (−2.13). Root r 0.19, thinning to 0.026 R.
unknowns: whether the glow is the Drive output

nodes.name: Drum rim plating
nodes.rationale: Hologram shows concentric horizontal bands on the funnel rather than vertical plates; 12 vertical segments are retained as a placeholder for the upper band only. Re-derive from an exterior frame. Re-purposed: the plating visible in #23 is on the drum rim wall and keel facets, not a separate lower-body plate ring.

nodes.name: Blade exit aperture
evidence: EPISODE_EVIDENCE_RICKMURAI_JACK.md (spacecraft launched from the bottom of the Citadel)
nodes.rationale: The spacecraft launches from the bottom (S05E10). With the keel resolved as a blade, the aperture is placed where the blade is still wide enough for the chute (z −1.0); exact exit point UNKNOWN.

nodes.name: Radial arm to DOME-S1

features: lenticular section: 0.55 R wide and 0.20 R thick at the equator, tapering to ≈0.2 R wide at ±0.10 R
cyan light strips along the edges (#23)
glazed skylight strip along the spine ridge (|side| < 0.07 R, above +0.095 R)
through-slot window band on both shoulders, r 1.40-1.75 (STL), glazed with vertical panes
interior: through-concourse 0 to +0.045, window galleries +0.0335 to +0.05 on the flanks at r 1.42-1.74 (STL slot level), utility deck below; exterior surface unchanged

interior_levels.name: through-concourse
interior_levels.use: the bridge itself, filling the full width of the section: the avenue road down the centre, the rail spur beside it on a low viaduct, walkways either side, and a low arcade of buildings along both flanks (bridge-side commerce); structural ribs follow the hull section; portal in the disc rim (r 0.995) and in the pod rim; lit by the spine skylight above and the shoulder window bands (the STL slot) at the pod end

interior_levels.name: window galleries
interior_levels.use: the STL slot floor at +0.0325 is a real surface over the concourse flanks at r 1.40-1.75; the space above it behind the window band is an observation gallery on each flank (the approach to the pod), reached by a stair/lift core at each end from the concourse

interior_levels.name: utility deck
interior_levels.use: services, freight and the Mortyburg disengage machinery at the root; continuous with the city sub-decks DK-1/DK-2 and the pod hull

nodes.rationale: Exterior #23 (third pass): the arms are long flat planks ≈0.35 R wide spanning ≈0.6 R between disc rim and pod rim, with cyan light strips along their sides, slightly below deck level. Numeric fit to #23: the arm slopes from the disc underside (z −0.03) down to the pod rim (z −0.28) over ≈0.85 R. Silhouette fit: arm width 0.44 R, sloping from z -0.03 at the disc to z -0.25 at the pod rim. STL: arc widths at the equator 0.50–0.66 R, 0.38–0.49 at −0.055, 0.20–0.25 at −0.096 and +0.10 — a lens-section bridge 0.2 R thick. Level with the deck, not sloping. The 0.2 R (400 m) section holds three enclosed levels; the through-concourse is at deck level so the city, arm and pod decks are one continuous floor. Nothing is added to the exterior surface.
unknowns: whether arms are level with the ground plane
required_shots: any exterior frame showing an arm

nodes.name: Principal transparent dome

features: smooth lens (half-ellipsoid) glazing, no cylindrical drum wall
raised circular hub at the apex (r ≈ 0.2 R)

nodes.rationale: STL cross-sections: the main body is a lens. Its upper surface rises from r = 1 at the equator to the apex 0.292 R above it, with r = 0.83 R at +0.15 and 0.90 R at +0.11 — fuller than a spherical cap. This replaces both the v1 hemisphere and the v2 spherical cap + drum. Existence A (exterior #23, hologram #04); geometry from the STL, a fan reconstruction, so the profile is B. Geometry measured from the STL.

nodes.name: Secondary dome 1

features: underside flush with the main hull (−0.10 R)

nodes.rationale: Exterior #23 (third pass, measured on the full frame): disc radius R = 80 px; pod diameter ≈ 100 px (near) / 100 px (far) → r ≈ 0.55 R; pod centres 150–210 px from the disc centre → ≈ 2.1 R allowing for perspective; pod rim depth ≈ 0.1 R. Hologram #04 agrees on topology. Azimuths relative to the interior UNKNOWN. Numeric fit to #23: pod centres at 2.39 R, radius 0.58 R, pod deck ≈0.3 R below the main deck (the arms slope down to them). Silhouette fit: pod radius 0.54, deck -0.31 below the main deck, cap height 0.1. Fitted per-pod centre distances were 2.73 / 2.14 / 2.67 R (near / far / right) with a long-lens camera being optimal, so the spread is a hand-drawn perspective artefact; symmetrised to 2.5 R. STL: pod centre at 2.316 R (az 36/156/276 in the STL frame), radius 0.592 R, apex +0.186 R, underside −0.10 R — the pods are scaled copies of the main lens sitting on the same equatorial plane. The silhouette fit's "pods hang 0.3 R lower" was an artefact of modelling the pods as caps on rims.
unknowns: whether it sits on the rim or projects from the lower body

Numeric fit to #23: pod centres at 2.39 R, radius 0.58 R, pod deck ≈0.3 R below the main deck (the arms slope down to them). nodes.name: Mortyburg dome (detachable section)

features: underside flush with the main hull (−0.10 R)

nodes.rationale: Mortyburg is a detachable domed section (A). #23 and #04 show all three satellite pods on arms; a pod on an arm is the only configuration that can disengage and fly off (S05E10), so Mortyburg = one of the three pods is now B. Which pod, and the azimuth, remain UNKNOWN. Numeric fit to #23: pod centres at 2.39 R, radius 0.58 R, pod deck ≈0.3 R below the main deck (the arms slope down to them). Silhouette fit: pod radius 0.54, deck -0.31 below the main deck, cap height 0.1. Fitted per-pod centre distances were 2.73 / 2.14 / 2.67 R (near / far / right) with a long-lens camera being optimal, so the spread is a hand-drawn perspective artefact; symmetrised to 2.5 R. STL: pod centre at 2.316 R (az 36/156/276 in the STL frame), radius 0.592 R, apex +0.186 R, underside −0.10 R — the pods are scaled copies of the main lens sitting on the same equatorial plane. The silhouette fit's "pods hang 0.3 R lower" was an artefact of modelling the pods as caps on rims. Mortyburg is one of these pods (B).

unknowns: whether it is glazed or solid

nodes.rationale: A square panel on a mast stands above one of the pods in #23 (solar array or antenna). Which pod is UNKNOWN.

nodes.name: Inner circumferential road
nodes.rationale: Several views show circular organisation. Three rings is a modelling convention, not a count from any frame.

nodes.name: Middle circumferential road
nodes.rationale: See CIRC-RING-1.

nodes.name: Outer circumferential road
nodes.rationale: See CIRC-RING-1.

nodes.name: Radial avenues (6; three aligned with the bridges)
nodes.rationale: Radial organisation is supported (B). Six avenues at 60 deg is the modelling convention chosen so that three of them run straight into the three bridge concourses (az 0, 120, 240) and continue as the bridge road onto the pod avenues; the other three are their continuations across the city.

nodes.name: Fifth and [Burp] Avenue intersection
nodes.rationale: Named intersection associated with Mortytown by dispatch; placed where CIRC-RING-2 meets the 225 deg radial, inside DIST-MORTYTOWN.

nodes.name: Commuter rail loop
nodes.rationale: A commuter train exists (A). A loop at z=+0.05 is a placeholder topology chosen so it can connect the plaza tramway to the Mortyburg spur; elevation is UNKNOWN (ground/elevated/underground all possible). Gallery #02 shows an elevated transit tube crossing a street, which supports (but does not prove) the elevated placement.
unknowns: whether the S03E07 train and S05E10 tram are the same system

nodes.name: Rail spur to Mortyburg
evidence: EPISODE_EVIDENCE_RICKMURAI_JACK.md (train route connecting affected area to Mortyburg)
nodes.rationale: Route exists and passes through the Mortyburg interface (A). Leaves the elevated loop at the Mortytown avenue, descends on columns to a low viaduct beside the avenue, passes the disc-rim portal, runs the bridge concourse on its left flank and enters the pod beside the pod avenue.
unknowns: whether the spur is the same track as the loop

nodes.name: Plaza tramway

features: sweeps around the plaza and out into the city

nodes.rationale: Tramway is shown in the same flooding sequence as the central plaza; therefore anchored adjacent to LM-CENTRAL-PLAZA. Direction is placeholder; drawn to meet CIRC-RAIL-LOOP. Gallery #14/#15 show the plaza ringed by curved cyan elevated tracks on slender columns at two or more heights; the tramway is therefore an elevated curved track around the plaza, not a ground path. Geometry changed from a straight ground path to an elevated ring segment.
unknowns: whether the S03E07 train runs on it

nodes.name: Hover / flying traffic band
nodes.rationale: Flying taxis and private flying cars exist (A). Band limits are a placeholder envelope for the 3D model's traffic layer. Envelope trimmed to r 0.8 / z 0.10 so the band stays under the glass (the lens is only 0.05 R tall at r 0.95). v2.5: the viewer no longer draws lanes or vehicles for it (owner request); the node remains as evidence of the traffic layer.
required_shots: S03E07 city montage with flying cars
S03E07 taxi pickup at Cafe Sanchez

nodes.name: Manhole / sewer access near plaza
evidence: EPISODE_EVIDENCE_RICKMURAI_JACK.md (manhole used by Rick and Morty)
nodes.rationale: Used during the plaza/tramway flooding sequence, so it sits at the plaza edge.

nodes.name: Citywide portal supply network
evidence: EPISODE_EVIDENCE_RICKMURAI_JACK.md (citywide portal supply can be hacked)
nodes.rationale: Exists as a system; no visible routing. Kept as a separate ID from UG-PORTAL-FLUID and UG-DIM-DRIVE per C-006.

nodes.name: Hover taxi service
nodes.rationale: Curbside pickup behaviour is direct evidence; vehicles are props on CIRC-HOVER-BAND / streets, not a placed structure.

nodes.name: Civic / government core
nodes.rationale: The central plaza and the Presidential Building are shown together in the collapse; government functions cluster around the plaza. Council Hall, courthouse and Morty Agency are placed here as PROVISIONAL/PLACEHOLDER, not because a frame shows them adjacent.
unknowns: which civic buildings are actually here

nodes.name: Commercial / high-rise ring
nodes.rationale: Dense high-rise blocks with storefronts, cafes and the newsroom. Ring placement is a convention: densest fabric between the civic core and the outer districts. Gallery #02 confirms very wide pedestrian streets flanked by monumental curved buildings with cyan strip lighting and at least one large dome-topped round building in the mid-ground.

nodes.name: High-status Rick residential
evidence: RICKLANTIS_VISUAL_EVIDENCE.md 2 (wealthy Rick in private flying car)
nodes.rationale: Stratification is documented; a distinct wealthy residential area is inferred, not shown as a district. Placed opposite Mortytown to express the contrast.
unknowns: whether a discrete district exists at all

nodes.name: East Sanchez Heights
nodes.rationale: Named subdivision (A). Placed on +X solely because of the word 'East' (C); 'Heights' suggests elevated terrain or towers (D).
unknowns: whether 'East' refers to Citadel geometry at all

nodes.name: Industrial sector
nodes.rationale: Simple Rick's and the Wishing Portal compound need large floor plates; grouped at the rim so heavy machinery can connect down to the lower body.
unknowns: whether industry is one sector or distributed

nodes.name: Mortytown
nodes.rationale: Distinct neighbourhood with streets, alleys, Morty Mart, Creepy Morty, occupied residences (A). Placed at the rim on a lower-status/edge inference (C). NOT the same thing as Mortyburg (C-003) — the sector is adjacent to the Mortyburg interface only as a modelling convenience.

nodes.name: Big Morty criminal territory
nodes.rationale: Criminal economy is shown inside Mortytown; the sub-sector is arbitrary.

nodes.name: Agricultural edge (MegaFruit farm)
nodes.rationale: Open agricultural land distinct from dense streets, previously identified as farm-at-edge; therefore an outer sector under the dome where open space reads correctly.
required_shots: S03E07 Farmer Rick and robot dog

nodes.name: Post-Rickshank construction zones
nodes.rationale: Damaged buildings and roadways with active skyscraper reconstruction (A). Where the damage was is UNKNOWN; the sector is arbitrary. In the 3D model this is a state-dependent overlay, not a permanent district.

nodes.name: Downtown Rickville (comic)
nodes.rationale: Comic-only location. Per C-008 it is not given animated-continuity coordinates.

nodes.name: Central plaza
nodes.rationale: S01E10 arrival frame (gallery #01) shows a large central atrium plaza under ribbed glazing with a monument tower at its centre, water and rock at its edge and curved multi-level walkways sweeping around it. Combined with the S05E10 "central plaza", the plaza is now carried through all intact states and anchored on the origin.
unknowns: whether the DS-01 atrium and the DS-04 plaza are the same space

nodes.name: Central monument tower (Rick statue)

features: late-era form: ornate pointed spire with arched base and orange detailing (#14/#15)

nodes.rationale: Directly visible at the centre of the arrival plaza in S01E10 (gallery #01): a tall pale spire with a Rick figure on it, walkways meeting it at height. Height ratio to people is roughly 25:1 in frame; 0.5 U is a placeholder. Survival after DS-02 UNKNOWN. Gallery #14/#15 (S05E10 plaza during the collapse) show an ornate pointed spire with arched base at the plaza centre, so a central spire persists into the late Citadel; its form differs from the S01E10 monument (rebuilt or re-dressed), which is why the node is carried through DS-03..05 rather than duplicated.
unknowns: whether the DS-01 and DS-04 spires are the same structure

nodes.name: Elevated curved walkways around the core
nodes.rationale: Gallery #01 shows at least three tiers of curved pedestrian walkways sweeping around the atrium at different heights. Modelled as one ring at z 0.12; add tiers once frames give the spacing.

nodes.name: Atrium water feature and rock garden
nodes.rationale: Water and large rocks flank the plaza on the left of the S01E10 arrival frame; confirms natural elements inside the civic core. Side is camera-relative, so the azimuth is placeholder. Gallery #15 shows a fountain pool with trees and planting in the late plaza, so the water feature persists (in some form) through DS-03..05.

nodes.name: Central spire cluster (DS-03 skyline)
nodes.rationale: The S03E07 streetscape (gallery #02) has a cluster of very tall spires on the vanishing point behind lower blocks; the tallest masses are therefore central, supporting the core-to-rim height gradient. Placed in the civic core; exact position UNKNOWN. Relaid 2026-09-12 (v2.4 layout audit): moved to a slot clear of the plaza, ring roads, radial avenues and neighbouring landmarks; still a convenience placement (class unchanged). v2.5: re-slotted clear of the six primary avenues (three aligned with the bridges), the ring-road bands and the elevated rail band.

nodes.name: Elevated transit tube crossing the street
nodes.rationale: Gallery #02 shows a horizontal transit tube/bridge spanning a pedestrian street at roughly 2-3 storeys. This is the first visual support for the rail loop being elevated; the loop stays PROVISIONAL at z 0.05 but the tube is logged as its own node until the two are proven the same.
unknowns: whether this is the commuter rail

nodes.name: Presidential Building
evidence: EPISODE_EVIDENCE_RICKMURAI_JACK.md (Rick and Morty exit it during the collapse)
nodes.rationale: Exited into the collapse sequence that also shows the plaza; placed on the plaza edge. Tallest civic mass by convention. Gallery #12 (dining room) shows a circular panoramic glazed room high above the skyline with spires and a domed building visible below, consistent with a tall building whose top level is a round glazed chamber. Relaid 2026-09-12 (v2.4 layout audit): moved to a slot clear of the plaza, ring roads, radial avenues and neighbouring landmarks; still a convenience placement (class unchanged). v2.5: re-slotted clear of the six primary avenues (three aligned with the bridges), the ring-road bands and the elevated rail band.

nodes.name: Domed building at the plaza edge
nodes.rationale: A large pale domed building with an orange roof stands at the plaza edge in the S05E10 collapse frames and a similar dome is visible from the Presidential dining room (#12). Side of the plaza is camera-relative, so the azimuth is placeholder. Relaid 2026-09-12 (v2.4 layout audit): moved to a slot clear of the plaza, ring roads, radial avenues and neighbouring landmarks; still a convenience placement (class unchanged). v2.5: re-slotted clear of the six primary avenues (three aligned with the bridges), the ring-road bands and the elevated rail band.
unknowns: whether it is the Council/Shadow Council hall

nodes.name: Council Hall (Council of Ricks)
nodes.rationale: Council chamber with stage/seating is direct (A). Its exterior and its position relative to the later Presidential Building are UNKNOWN. Placed in the civic core. States end at DS-02 because the Council is destroyed in Rickshank; whether the building persists is UNKNOWN. Gallery #24 (S01E10) shows the civic building the arriving Ricks face: a broad multi-storey glazed façade with three large emblem banners, a grand stair, a domed turret and tall spires behind. Identified as the Council building by the Council-era emblem; position still not shown. Relaid 2026-09-12 (v2.4 layout audit): moved to a slot clear of the plaza, ring roads, radial avenues and neighbouring landmarks; still a convenience placement (class unchanged). v2.5: re-slotted clear of the six primary avenues (three aligned with the bridges), the ring-road bands and the elevated rail band.

Gallery #26 (S03E01) shows the tribunal form: a raised yellow curved dais bearing the Council emblem, an audience floor below, and a giant oval feature wall behind.

nodes.name: Dimensional Drive chamber

features: long straight suspended walkway/bridge over void (#13)

nodes.rationale: Secondary sources describe the Drive as central; its failure deforms the whole Citadel, consistent with a central position. Anchored on the axis below the civic core. The funnel form (hologram #04) puts the widest underground volume just below the city and narrows towards the apex: the Drive fits the upper funnel, the launch chamber and chute the neck. Gallery #13 shows a long straight suspended platform/bridge over a dark void with the Central Finite Curve portal-spiral projected beside it; #17 shows a rail cart running on a curved rail in the same environment. The chamber is therefore a large void spanned by walkways, not a solid machinery block.

procedural.note: Parameters for schematic/viewer/interior.js. Generated fill is not evidence; see INTERIOR.md.

families.DIST-AGRICULTURAL: no buildings: fields, water, trees, farmhouse
families.pods: generic mid-rise; DOME-MB uses the Mortytown family

arm_section.note: STL arm cross-section at mid-arm (r 1.35 R), perpendicular to the arm axis: [z/R, half-width/R]. Underside −0.108, top +0.12 (mid) to +0.15 (root). From reference_models/STL_MEASUREMENTS.md.
arm_section.surface_notes: STL top surface z(side) at r 1.1-1.7 on all three arms: smooth lens with a central spine ridge. The section is narrowest at r 1.30 (half-width 0.249 R at the equator) and flares to 0.31 R at the disc fillet and 0.34 R at the pod fillet. From r 1.40 to 1.75 a horizontal slot is cut through both shoulders (floor +0.0335 R, ceiling rising to +0.0575 R): the flat "shelf" reported in v2.4 is the floor of this slot, i.e. the window band. Fin faces are smooth tapers with no recess.

windows.evidence: the STL cuts a horizontal slot into both shoulders of each arm from r 1.40 to 1.75 under an overhanging upper slab: floor at z +0.0335 R, ceiling rising from +0.035 at r 1.40 to +0.0575 at r 1.725, the slot running inward to a 0.094 R spine; the Printables render paints the openings teal; frame #23 shows a row of lit strips on the arm flanks beside the pods
windows.placement: vertical glazing panes in the face of the overhanging upper slab (|side| ~0.18-0.19 R, measured from the section just above the slot ceiling), both shoulders, r 1.42-1.74, height = slot height at that r (2 m at the root of the slot to 48 m by the pod); the flat shelf outside the slab face (|side| 0.19-0.26+) is a ledge in front of the windows
windows.confidence: existence A (frame + STL slot), placement A (slot measured)

skylight.status: design decision on the owner's request (2026-09-12); placement class C
skylight.rule: STL arm triangles within |side| < 0.07 R of the spine and above z +0.095 R render as glazing; every other arm triangle stays hull
skylight.evidence: the STL carries a raised spine ridge along each arm top and the Printables render shows a lighter centre strip there; frame #23 shows the arms lit from within; no frame shows the arm roof directly, so the strip is not promoted above C

half_width_by_r.note: STL cross-sections perpendicular to the arm axis, all three arms identical to 0.001 R; half-width of the solid at each z (R units), by r along the arm. Rows inside the shoulder slot (r >= 1.40, z ~0.033-0.058) show the spine only (0.047).

shell.note: ray probes across the embedded STL show two surfaces ~0.005 R apart on the arm flanks: the model is a thin shell, not a solid; interior structure is inset >= 0.018 R from the outer surface

rib_profiles.note: interior rib profiles: convex hull of the STL section polygon at each r (the section carries a shallow groove at each equator edge, the light-strip channel, which the ribs ignore), offset inward by 0.013 R (shell ~0.005 + tube radius 0.004 + margin), sampled at 64 points by arc length; arm-local (side, z) in R units

top_surface.note: STL top-surface height (R units) by ray cast straight down, arm-local grid: r along the arm, side across it; used to lay the skylight frame and mullions on the real surface
